Re-derived independently from the shards (not inherited from batch 1's draft): the clause's obligations are SESSION-SURVIVAL obligations, not stream-handling ones. lesson-experience.md REQ-LX-03 (lines 36-46) states the obligation set (stay mounted across beat transitions, never display:none, never zero height, min-height for xterm fit() safety) and then vests instance ownership in the PersistentTerminalHost; terminal-experience.md REQ-TX-01 (lines 11-21) scopes that host to XTERM instances - all three scenarios are xterm/session-shaped (same instance with scrollback across route changes, scrollback restore via @xterm/addon-serialize plus event-log replay for the gap, WebGL context-loss fallback without losing the session); docs/origin/GLOSSARY.md line 23 defines a persistent beat as one that stays mounted across navigation 'xterm safety by construction'. So the compiler's question is 'is there a session identity to restore?', never 'do bytes arrive over time?'. Empirically confirmed the request-scoped premise rather than assuming it: src/app/api/playground/run/route.ts builds a per-request ReadableStream returned with Content-Type text/event-stream and carries NO session identifier (lines 62-112) - the run completes, output becomes ordinary client state, nothing to reattach to, no scrollback to serialize, no xterm to fit().
